chakariaAnwara.name: Chakaria to Anwara, and Maheshkhali-Kutubdia Islands

chittagongNoakhali.name: Chittagong to Noakhali
chittagongNoakhali.note: k = 0.33: the Chittagong end is on the Chittagong-Cox's Bazar-Teknaf coast (0.5), the Noakhali end is not; the smaller rate (the higher surge inland) is taken for the whole region

sandwipHatiya.name: Sandwip, Hatiya and all islands in this region

notes.waterLevelReturnPeriod: Table 6.2.26 notes (p. 672) give the 50-year column for category IV and the 100-year one for I-III, the reverse of Sec 2.6.3 (p. 667) and of the notes of Table 6.2.25 (p. 671); the larger 100-year level is taken for every category (the more conservative reading)
notes.flotationFactor: SAEngine practice, not BNBC: Sec 1.6.4 asks the building to resist flotation but gives no factor; the factor of safety of 1.5 of Sec 1.6.4 against overturning and sliding is used for flotation too
notes.shelter: Table 6.2.28 rows read '< 2' and '3 - 4' storeys; 2 storeys falls in neither, so it takes the larger 34 kN/m² (the more conservative reading); the text of Sec 2.6.7.1 cites the table as 6.2.27
notes.explosion: Figure 6.2.33(a) digitised at the axis ticks 1/30 ... 1/5 (its scale is not linear); 70 kN/m² below 1/30, the figure ends at 1/5 (held beyond, with a note); a guide only (Sec 2.6.6.1 (b))

sources.returnPeriod: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 2.6.3 (p. 667): 100-year values for essential facilities and the hazardous facilities of Table 6.1.1, 50-year for other structures
sources.waterUnitWeight: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 2.6.3.4.1 (p. 674): γw = 9.80 kN/m³ fresh water, 10.05 kN/m³ salt water
sources.surgeRegions: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Table 6.2.25 (p. 670); Eq 6.2.71 hs = hT - (x - 1)k, k = 0.5 for the Chittagong-Cox's Bazar-Teknaf coast and 0.33 for other coastal areas (p. 670)
sources.waterLevels: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Table 6.2.26 (pp. 671-672): extreme surface water levels above PWD datum during monsoon; Eq 6.2.70 hf = yT - yg; Eq 6.2.69 Hm = max(hs, hf) (p. 668)
sources.freeWaterIncrease: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 2.6.3.2.1 (p. 670): surfaces exposed to free water, design depth Hm + 0.30 m
sources.hydrodynamic: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 2.6.3.2.2 (pp. 672-673): wave amplitude hw = hs/4 ≥ 1 m; wind 80 or 90 m/s; V ≤ 3.0 m/s: equivalent surcharge dh = aV²/2g (Eq 6.2.72), a ≥ 1.25, ds ≤ V ≤ √(g ds)
sources.breakingWave: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 2.6.3.4-2.6.3.4.2 (pp. 674-676): Hb = 0.78 ds (Eq 6.2.73), ds = 0.65 Hm (Eq 6.2.74), FD = 0.5 γw CD D Hb² (Eq 6.2.75), Pmax = Cp γw ds + 1.2 γw ds (Eq 6.2.76), Ft = 1.1 Cp γw ds² + 2.4 γw ds² (Eq 6.2.77) or + 1.9 γw ds² with water behind (Eq 6.2.78)
sources.stabilityFactor: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 1.6.4 (p. 501): overturning and sliding under wind and flood or surge together, factor of safety 1.5 on dead load only
sources.rain: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 1.6.5 (p. 501), Sec 2.6.2.1-2.6.2.2 (p. 667): all the rainwater to the level of the secondary drainage with the primary drains blocked, plus 0.25 kN/m² with controlled drainage; ponding instability considered; γw of Sec 2.6.3.4.1 (p. 674)
sources.helipad: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 2.6.8 Eqs 6.2.82a-c (p. 683): L1 = W1 on the contact areas, L2 = k W2 on 300 mm × 300 mm (k 0.75 hydraulic shock absorbers, 1.5 rigid or skid gear), L3 = 5.0 kN/m²
sources.explosion: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 2.6.6.1-2.6.6.3, Figure 6.2.33 (pp. 680-682): q0 by A0/v, vent glass breaking at 4 kN/m²; least internal pressure or suction 5 kN/m²; relief vents at 1.0 kN/m²
